title: Virtual Head Attention: Smashing the Attention Trilemma

beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how Virtual Head Attention cuts 84.4% of memory overhead.

beats.text: Standard GQA hogs memory, while MLA sacrifices accuracy. It is a zero-sum game of architectural compromise.
beats.visual_focus: Side-by-side comparison of GQA and MLA memory footprints.

beats.text: Virtual Head Attention breaks the cycle using Q-Premix and Linear Postmix to simulate diversity without adding heads.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—straight to the point, no 'Hey guys' fluff. I liked that you actually named the trade-offs instead of just saying 'it's fast.' However, when you mentioned Q-Premix and Linear Postmix in Beat 3, I had to pause to think if those were standard terms or specific to this paper. Since I'm scrolling, I don't have time to look up the paper mid-video. If you're going to use proprietary terms, give me a one-second hint of what they actually do to the tensors.

Long-context models are trapped: you can have memory, compute, or quality. Pick two, lose one.

Why is Virtual Head Attention a major breakthrough? Because the design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until Virtual Head Attention proved: gQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute.
